newsitem.title: UK: Mirror Group bids for Midland Independent.
newsitem.headline: Mirror Group bids for Midland Independent.

text.p: British newspaper company Mirror Group Plc said on Friday it agreed to buy Midland Independent Newspapers Plc in a deal worth about 297 million pounds ($501.2 million).
Mirror Group said it was offering 210 pence per share for Midland versus Thursday's closing price of 188.5.
The bid represented a 41 percent premium over Midland's closing price on June 16, the day before the companies announced they were in merger talks.
Midland's shares firmed 3.0 pence to 191-1/2 by 0725 GMT, while Mirror's shares were flat at 186.
Mirror said it had already agreed to buy 14.9 percent of Midland from certain shareholders at a price of 210 pence per share.
Mirror Group said the acquisition would beef up its presence in central England's Midlands region, where about 10 percent of Mirror's newspapers are circulated.
For its part, Midland predicted its pre-tax profit before exceptional items would not be less than 13.2 million pounds for the half year to June 29.
The firm expected to pay an interim dividend of 2.0 pence and a second interim payout of 3.0 pence later this year or early next year.
The acquisition would hinge on clearance by the Department for Trade and Industry.
Mirror said it did not expect a DTI decision on the deal before October.
Midland chief executive Chris Oakley will join Mirror's board after the deal, while chairman Sir Norman Fowler will head a new regional board for the Midlands.
